body.title: Panchakroshi Yatra: The 50-Mile Sacred Circumambulation of Kashi
body.orientation: How an ancient circular pilgrimage route traces the cosmic perimeter of Varanasi and preserves its sacred mandala.

hero.alt: Pilgrims circumambulating sacred shrines in the Varanasi hinterland

paragraphs.text: The Panchakroshi Yatra is a traditional pilgrimage covering a perimeter of approximately 50 miles (5 kroshas radius) encompassing the sacred field of Kashi.
The pilgrimage typically takes five days on foot, visiting 108 principal shrines located in five major halting camps before concluding at Manikarnika Ghat.
Described in the medieval Kashi Khanda text, the route transforms the physical countryside into a living mandala where every step earns the spiritual merit of traversing the universe.
Panchakroshi illustrates how sacred geography in India integrates rural landscape, temple architecture, and walking ritual into an unbroken living practice.
